# Live stack: how loud the incidents are (RP-19)

200 incidents, 8 services each. Peak shift is the largest robust z of any of a service's metrics after the fault, against its own pre-fault window.

| Fault | Median peak, root (σ) | Median peak, other services (σ) |
|---|---:|---:|
| all | 2,711.1 | 18.2 |
| cpu | 474.2 | 22.4 |
| delay | 2,858.0 | 34.7 |
| mem | 2,058.7 | 5.4 |
| release | 404,750.0 | 10.3 |

| Threshold | Services crossing it, mean per incident |
|---|---:|
| 2σ | 8.00 of 8 |
| 10σ | 5.55 of 8 |
| 100σ | 2.54 of 8 |

The steady synthetic load leaves near-flat baselines, so even services the fault never reached shift by tens of σ. At 2σ, the count of anomalous services in the realism table is therefore saturated and is not evidence about propagation. This is consistent with the Kaal-trained ranker failing here: its topology features read *which* services are anomalous, and here that is all of them. The rankers that compare *how much* each service moved (loudest, RCAEval-trained) keep their signal. A consistent account, not a tested one.
